meta.title: HiveSpace architecture
meta.subtitle: Container view of the MVP: the gateway/BFF, nine services, the image Function, the event bus and the externals. Click a component, arrow or pin; pick a flow to follow one scenario. Every service has its own database (shown in its sub-label), never read by another service.
meta.description: Buyers, sellers and the operator reach a single gateway/BFF that serves the SPAs and forwards REST calls to nine services. Services call each other with gRPC and exchange events through Azure Service Bus with outbox and inbox. An Azure Function processes uploaded images in blob storage. Externals: payment provider, Google, LLM, email.
overview: REST at the edge, gRPC inside (ADR-0019)
Postgres per service, MongoDB for Cart, Blob
Container Apps, scale to zero; Aspire locally
meta.footnote: Source: docs/architecture.md (sections 5–6, 11) and ADR-0001…0026. gRPC and event arrows are drawn for the main relations; the full lists are in the tables below. Generated with html-flow-diagram; edit architecture-flow.model.json and rebuild.

nodes.label: Seller
nodes.desc: Manages a shop, products, stock and orders in the seller centre (/seller).

nodes.label: Buyer / Visitor
nodes.desc: Browses, searches, keeps a cart, checks out and pays.

nodes.label: Operator
nodes.desc: The builder: seeds data, drives the mock payment and shipping controls during demos.

nodes.label: Web SPAs
nodes.desc: Storefront (/) and seller centre (/seller). Static files served from the gateway image; generated API client; vue-i18n.

nodes.label: Gateway + BFF
nodes.sub: .NET · YARP · one public origin · encrypted cookie · token relay · rate limits · anonymous callback route
nodes.desc: The only external ingress. Confidential OIDC client and BFF: tokens stay server-side in an encrypted HttpOnly cookie; relays a bearer token to services; CSRF header, rate limits, correlation ID (ADR-0008).

nodes.label: Media
nodes.desc: Upload intents, SAS issuing and media records (pending, ready, rejected, detached).

nodes.label: Catalog
nodes.desc: Category tree, products, variants, reviews and rating aggregates.

nodes.label: Inventory
nodes.desc: On-hand, reserved, available; atomic reservations with lazy expiry (ADR-0007).

nodes.label: Order
nodes.desc: Checkout saga, orders, status timeline, mock shipping, pricing pipeline (ADR-0006).

nodes.label: Cart
nodes.desc: Cart lines per user and cart display composition; one document per user (ADR-0017, ADR-0018).

nodes.label: Payment
nodes.desc: Payments, refunds, ledger, IPaymentProvider (mock, VNPay optional), callback endpoint (ADR-0004).

nodes.label: Identity
nodes.desc: OIDC authorization server: users, credentials, external logins, profile, addresses, shop (ADR-0008).

nodes.label: Search-AI
nodes.desc: Product read model, full-text index, embeddings, keyword and NL search (ADR-0003, ADR-0014).

nodes.label: Notification
nodes.desc: Contact projection, templates (vi, en), email records with retries and dedupe (ADR-0016).

nodes.label: Event bus
nodes.sub: Azure Service Bus · topic hivespace-events · outbox → bus → inbox · at-least-once
nodes.desc: IEventBus over Service Bus (emulator locally, RabbitMQ optional). JSON envelope, trace context in the envelope, consumers dedupe by eventId (ADR-0002).

nodes.label: Image processor
nodes.desc: Triggered by MediaUploaded: validates the signature, re-encodes, strips metadata, resizes, writes to the public container (ADR-0011).

nodes.label: Blob storage
nodes.desc: Azure Blob (Azurite locally): private incoming container, public read container, gateway data-protection keys.

nodes.label: Payment provider
nodes.desc: Mock provider (lives in the Payment service) or VNPay sandbox. Sends signed callbacks.

nodes.label: Google
nodes.desc: Social sign-in behind IExternalLoginProvider; only the Google button fails if it is down (FR-AUTH-023).

nodes.label: LLM + embeddings
nodes.desc: Query interpretation and embeddings behind ILlmProvider / IEmbeddingProvider; runtime undecided (ADR-0014, OQ-4).

nodes.label: Email provider
nodes.desc: IEmailSender: Mailpit locally, Resend in the demo.

all.title: HiveSpace: overall architecture
all.intro: Gateway/BFF in front of nine services and one Function. REST at the edge, gRPC between services, events through the bus. Pick a flow to see one scenario.

register.title: Register and verify email
register.intro: UC-001: the first cross-stack event path (FEAT-001).

steps.t: Visitor registers: the storefront posts to /v1/users through the gateway.
Identity commits the user, credential, token hash and UserRegistered in one transaction; the outbox relays it.
Notification consumes it once (inbox) and records the email.
Verification email goes out in the registration language.

signin.title: Sign in through the BFF (password or Google)
signin.intro: UC-002, UC-025, ADR-0008. The browser never sees a token.

steps.t: /bff/login starts the OIDC code flow with PKCE.
Identity authorizes: password check with lockout, or…
Continue with Google: code exchange, verified email required to auto-link.
Gateway stores tokens in the encrypted cookie and returns to the SPA.

checkout.title: Checkout with stock reservation and compensation
checkout.intro: UC-011: orchestrated saga in Order (ADR-0006, ADR-0007).

steps.t: POST /v1/checkouts with an Idempotency-Key; Order starts the saga.
Gather selected cart lines, authoritative prices and the address snapshot.
Reserve all lines atomically in Inventory; any shortfall fails the checkout with no orders.
Online payment is initiated; a failure releases the reservation and compensates.
Events: CheckoutCompleted clears the cart; OrderPlaced commits the reservation (COD).

payment.title: Payment callback, delivered three times
payment.intro: UC-012, NFR-REL-003, ADR-0004: one payment effect, one order transition.

steps.t: Payment created at the provider; the buyer pays there.
Signed callback arrives on the anonymous gateway route and is forwarded to Payment.
One transaction: unique provider-event row, compare-and-set PENDING → PAID, outbox. Duplicates are acknowledged and ignored.
Order moves AWAITING_PAYMENT → PLACED and publishes OrderPlaced.
Inventory commits the reservation.

search.title: Natural-language search with keyword fallback
search.intro: UC-008: the LLM is optional; a timeout or bad output falls back to keyword search.

steps.t: Read model: Catalog publishes versioned ProductChanged; Search-AI indexes it.
GET /v1/search/nl, rate limited at the gateway.
Interpret and embed (3 s timeout, fixed schema); on failure, keyword search on the raw query.

media.title: Image upload through a presigned URL
media.intro: ADR-0011: the browser uploads straight to blob; the Function validates before anything is public.

steps.t: Upload intent: Media returns a write-only SAS URL.
Browser PUTs the bytes into the private container.
MediaUploaded triggers the image processor.
Validate and re-encode into the public container; Media marks the record ready.

notes.b: Tokens stay server-side in an encrypted cookie; the browser never holds a token. Services still validate the JWT and enforce roles.
Limits are wrong with 2+ replicas; pin the gateway to one replica.
State persisted after every step; a crash resumes or compensates on the next wake. 0 orphan orders under failure injection.
Conditional update on sorted rows in one transaction; lazy expiry is the final backstop.
Unique provider-event row in the same transaction as the status change.
Standard tier is billed per hour while the namespace exists (~$10/month if left up). Provision per deploy window, amend the budget, or swap to RabbitMQ.
Verification and reset tokens are in the event payload. Hash-only storage in Identity, never logged, outbox rows deleted after 24 h.
Pick the LLM and embedding provider; store the model ID with every vector.
Atlas free tier or Cosmos DB for MongoDB; Cart stays on single-document atomic updates.
App scale-from-zero + Neon wake + Function start can miss the 5 s image target. Warm the stack before demos.
9 services, 1 Function, 3 stacks against ~390 hours. Cut order: Media + Function, then Notification into Order, then Cart into Order. Never the saga or inventory.
Services trust the network plus a validated JWT; no mTLS or service identity. Acceptable for a demo with no real money.
Add VerificationEmailRequested to the event catalog and amend ADR-0008's hosted-pages bullet (auth screens are SPA pages).
